transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Menon (Hanover CTO), Samir Gupta (Head of ML), Asha Iyer (Hanover PMM)

[00:00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, welcome, this is Lena at Redwood, super excited to have Hanover on. We're doing a short fireside chat today — just friendly, a few stories and some quotes we can use for a case study and a short promo. Thanks for joining.

[00:00:15] Dr. Priya Menon: Thanks Lena, happy to be here. Um, Samir and I are, you know, excited to share a bit of what we've been working on, it's been a wild ride.

[00:00:24] Samir Gupta: Yeah hi all, Samir here. Quick note — I'm in New Jersey so slight lag if I disappear, but all good.

[00:00:30] Marcus Chen: Quick intro from me, Marcus, I work on performance and bringing on customers' model stacks onto Redwood. I'll chime in with metrics when useful.

[00:00:40] Asha Iyer: And I'm Asha, product marketing at Hanover, I'm helping coordinate the case study side.

[00:00:48] Lena Park: Great. Maybe Priya, can you kick off with a bit of context — what problem were you trying to solve and what led you to consider Redwood?

[00:00:58] Dr. Priya Menon: Sure. So at Hanover we're building automated clinical summaries for discharge notes and specialist referrals. The main pain was twofold: one, inference cost — we run millions of tokens a day — and two, latency requirements for interactive clinician tools, like the quick-summary widget in the EHR. We tried hosting models ourselves on MajorCloud but the ops burden and the variability in latency were — uh — heavy. Plus we needed to meet SOC 2 requirements for logs and encryption.

[00:01:32] Samir Gupta: To add, we had a mixture of model sizes — a few Llama-family models for shorter summaries and an LLM fine-tuned for clinical style for long-form summarization. Running them in the same infra was messy — memory pinning and KV cache thrashing, especially at peak.

[00:01:49] Lena Park: Makes sense. Marcus, you ran the initial benchmark with their stack, do you want to summarize the findings?

[00:01:55] Marcus Chen: Yeah, quick one — we replicated their ensemble locally and on Redwood. Baseline: self-hosted on MajorCloud with a standard 8-GPU pool, averaged 520 ms p50 latency on the short path and 1.8s p50 for long-form. Cost per 1k tokens was around $0.45 after reserved discounts. On Redwood, after enabling batching + prefix KV caching and switching to a quantized variant for the short models, we saw p50 drop to ~210 ms and long-form to ~1.1s. Token cost dropped to ~ $0.32 per 1k, and with additional compile kernels we got throughput improvements of roughly 2x on peak workloads.

[00:02:39] Dr. Priya Menon: Those numbers look right. The big win for us was consistency — the variance tightened, so clinicians didn't see the UI hang randomly. We also liked the private deployment option; our security team insisted on SSO and KMS integration which Redwood supported.

[00:02:57] Asha Iyer: Could you say more about the quantization tradeoffs? We want a simple quote about quality vs cost.

[00:03:03] Samir Gupta: Sure — so we tried INT8 and an 8-bit quantized float path. There was a tiny uptick in hallucination for the longest, very specialized discharge narratives, but for the 80% of queries that are short clinical summaries quality stayed the same subjectively. We paired that with regression tests in our eval harness — Redwood's rollouts and automatic fallback to full-precision helped a lot. For the case study we can say: "Adopted quantized short-path models for 80% of traffic, preserving quality while reducing token cost."

[00:03:36] Lena Park: Nice. Did you run into any setup surprises with the VPC/private deployment?

[00:03:40] Dr. Priya Menon: A couple of network routing minutiae — our firewall rules initially blocked the internal health checks. But Redwood's onboarding docs + Marcus' hands-on help got us past it. Also we asked for additional audit log retention on some endpoints for certain clients and Redwood enabled extended retention via the console.

[00:04:00] Marcus Chen: We also added a small routing policy so that if the private pool saturated we could failover to a dedicated hosted pool in another region, with strict redaction on PII — that helped during our first busy day.

[00:04:12] Samir Gupta: On the topic of failover, curious — any cost surprises during that temporary failover?

[00:04:17] Marcus Chen: It did spike a touch because the hosted pool was less quantized for the long path, but the policy limited the duration and we observed it in the cost dashboard within minutes. The ability to see token-level cost and attribute to routes was huge for finance.

[00:04:33] Lena Park: This is great color — Asha, for marketing, any specific angle you'd like to highlight?

[00:04:38] Asha Iyer: We're leaning into "reliability at scale for clinical workflows" and a concrete number helps, so that 30% token-cost reduction and 2x throughput stat — could we lock those down for a headline?

[00:04:50] Dr. Priya Menon: Yes, you can use those. To be precise: total token cost down roughly 30% after moving to Redwood defaults plus additional caching. Throughput during typical peak windows increased by ~2x after batching and kernel tuning.

[00:05:02] Lena Park: Great quote! Any hesitation about naming Redwood in the case study?

[00:05:06] Dr. Priya Menon: No, we're fine. Legal will do a quick sign-off but I'm comfortable.

[00:05:12] Samir Gupta: Quick technical note — during rollout we used per-prompt routing rules so triage prompts went to the non-quantized long-path model, that reduced regressions. Might be a decent small technical callout in the appendix.

[00:05:25] Lena Park: We'll add that as a short technical sidebar. Marcus, do you have any prod incident anecdotes that are safe to share?

[00:05:31] Marcus Chen: One — during a vendor SDK update the auto-batching library had a minor regression and p95 spiked, we rolled back the patch and pinned the scheduler config; that was more ops hygiene than Redwood-specific but it shows the value of the Canary deploys and the traffic replay we used to validate.

[00:05:53] Asha Iyer: Love that. For the promo clip, we want a 30-45s soundbite — Priya, would you be comfortable with a short on-camera 20–30 second comment about clinician experience improvements?

[00:06:05] Dr. Priya Menon: Yeah, I can do that. Something like: "Our clinicians now get reliable, readable summaries in under a second — it saves time at the point of care and reduces cognitive load."

[00:06:16] Lena Park: Perfect. We'll capture B-roll and ship a proposed script.

[00:06:21] Samir Gupta: One quick question for Marcus — you mentioned KV caching. How often do we need to warm the cache and any risk of staleness for clinical prompts?

[00:06:29] Marcus Chen: We tuned the prefix cache TTL to 24 hours for structured prompts and 6 hours for free text. Because summaries are often templated around diagnosis codes, the cache hit rate was ~45% during daytime peaks, which is what moved the cost needle. Staleness was minimal because we included a short checksum on the prompt template and invalidated when template versions changed.

[00:06:53] Dr. Priya Menon: That checksum trick was a lifesaver.

[00:06:57] Lena Park: This is all very useful. Any competitors or alternatives you evaluated?

[00:07:03] Samir Gupta: We looked at MajorCloudAI's managed endpoints and an open-source orchestration project, OpenServeAI. MajorCloudAI had similar raw performance but their billing model made forecasting harder; OpenServeAI was attractive but not mature enough operationally.

[00:07:19] Lena Park: Understood. Before we wrap, any remaining asks from marketing or engineering sides?

[00:07:24] Asha Iyer: We'll need a two-paragraph testimonial and a headshot from Priya. Also Marcus, if you can give a one-page tech sidebar that Asha can use in the PDF case study, that'd be helpful.

[00:07:36] Marcus Chen: Yep will do.

[00:07:39] Dr. Priya Menon: I'll get legal to triage but should be quick.

[00:07:44] Lena Park: Awesome — recap of next steps: Lena to draft case study and send to Priya; Marcus to export cost/latency dashboards and a one-pager; Priya to review and sign off; schedule a short video recording. Anything else?

[00:07:58] Samir Gupta: Maybe a short note for engineering folks — we'll share the per-route config JSON and the perf scripts.

[00:08:06] Lena Park: Good call. Ok folks, huge thanks, this was super helpful and we'll follow up with the assets.

[00:08:12] Dr. Priya Menon: Thanks everyone.

[00:08:15] Asha Iyer: Thanks!

[00:08:17] Marcus Chen: Bye all.

[00:08:20] Lena Park: Bye!
